source_code_evidence.note: Upper bounds are code-path maxima, not claims that every case reached the maximum.

findings: `-f/--from-file` reads multiple patterns and is documented as much faster than invoking apt-file many times.
`-x/--regexp` is documented as potentially rather slow; the manpage recommends non-regex matching plus downstream filtering when performance matters.
`--stream-results` can reduce memory use and time to first result when automated consumers can tolerate duplicate matches.

causal_reconciliation: The timed-out PR79 implementation repeatedly rescans the apt Contents indices through separate regex subprocesses.
The same implementation can launch a very large remote manpage enrichment fanout after preliminary candidate generation.
The apt-file supplier itself exposes a purpose-built multi-pattern path specifically to avoid repeated invocations and documents regex mode as a performance risk.
Therefore a numeric micro-profile is not required to justify replacing the structurally dominated acquisition mechanism; the failed profile surface is quarantined rather than retried.

repair_principles: Use one apt-file multi-pattern invocation per effect rather than one regex process per semantic term.
Prefer literal/substr matching and post-filter executable paths/command names in-process.
Treat manpage retrieval as bounded progressive enrichment, not a blanket fanout over the full preliminary set.
Cache command/manpage evidence by stable command/distribution identity inside the process and across repeated tasks when durable cache is available.
Preserve zero package hints and task-specific literals.
